questions: Does “must be present in order to give rise to a licensing obligation” state a sufficient trigger, or only a necessary threshold whose satisfaction leaves further requirements unresolved?

assumptions: This predicate concerns the selected applicability condition, not whole-law compliance or licence possession.
Case-dependent input classifications and incorporated authority remain external to the encoded predicate.
The declared input vocabulary is supplied for this controlled comparison; its adequacy as a legal abstraction remains unverified.
“Which” refers to all three enumerated factors, and “at least one” permits any nonempty combination.
The final “and” completes the enumeration; it does not override the expressly stated minimum of one.

For this reading, the introductory reference to determination by these factors makes their disjunction the selected trigger, although treating the threshold as sufficient requires an interpretive assumption.

citations.quote: three key factors, at least one of which must be present in order to give rise to a licensing obligation
secondly, the family office is carrying on a business in the provision of such services; and thirdly, the business is carried on in Hong Kong.

readings.distinction: Inclusive disjunction understood as the selected trigger. True means at least one supplied factor is satisfied. An all-three conjunction is not a defensible local parse merely because the enumeration ends with “and”; it would displace the explicit “at least one” threshold.

citations.quote: at least one of which must be present in order to give rise to a licensing obligation

readings.distinction: The connective remains inclusive disjunction, but its modal role changes: a licensing obligation requires this threshold, while the threshold alone need not establish the trigger. This is the more cautious grammatical reading of “must ... in order to”. Both readings therefore have the same antecedent predicate, with an unresolved difference in sufficiency.

vocabulary_concerns: The three Boolean facts express threshold satisfaction but cannot encode whether that threshold is necessary or sufficient for a licensing obligation. Identical antecedent expressions do not resolve this modal disagreement.

“That business” makes hong_kong refer back to the business described by business. The vocabulary supplies no consistency rule for these related classifications; no independence assumption or truth assignment has been added.

The case-dependent classifications, ordinary-course qualification, and regulatory-intent discussion in Q3 cannot be reconstructed from these three Booleans. They remain external qualifications rather than invented exceptions to the explicit disjunction.
